question: Should OpenClaw add a native ASR/STT backend abstraction for platform voice input, and which first flow should own the custom endpoint contract?
rationale: The request is valid, but implementation changes native capture, provider routing, credentials, private-network access, and fallback behavior; automation cannot choose that product and security boundary safely.

options.title: Design native STT seam first
options.body: Start with a maintainer-scoped native ASR/STT abstraction, likely macOS Push-to-Talk or native Talk first, and bridge to `tools.media.audio` or provider contracts only through the chosen boundary.

options.title: Keep this plugin/provider-only
options.body: Close or narrow the native request if maintainers decide existing realtime provider plugins and ClawHub should own custom ASR and native app capture should stay platform-speech-only.

options.title: Defer custom ASR endpoints
options.body: Keep the issue open but intentionally defer implementation until security, UX, and platform support requirements are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design native STT seam first
recommendation.body: Start with a maintainer-scoped native ASR/STT abstraction, likely macOS Push-to-Talk or native Talk first, and bridge to `tools.media.audio` or provider contracts only through the chosen boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest native voice feature-history signal and is already connected to the issue timeline.
